gaps.sentence: Try to be ___ when you cross the busy road (CARE).
gaps.explanation: An adjective is needed after 'be': careful (-ful). 'Carefully' is an adverb and cannot follow 'be'.

gaps.sentence: The success of the launch rests on the ___ (RELY) of the supplier.
gaps.explanation: 'The reliability of the supplier' — the quality noun is needed after 'the'.

gaps.sentence: It is almost ___ to park in the city centre (POSSIBLE).
gaps.hint: negative adjective needed — parking is extremely difficult
gaps.explanation: The in- of 'possible' becomes im- before p: impossible. The context shows a negative meaning.

gaps.sentence: Don't ___ your children — let them make their own mistakes (PROTECT).
gaps.hint: protect too much (over-); a base verb is needed
gaps.explanation: The prefix over- means excessively: overprotect means to protect too much. A base verb follows 'Don't'.

gaps.sentence: The company is a major ___ (EMPLOY) in the region.
gaps.hint: the company gives jobs — it is the one who employs
gaps.explanation: An employer gives work; an employee receives it. The sentence is about the company.

gaps.sentence: The government wants to ___ the tax system (SIMPLE).
gaps.explanation: The suffix -ify forms the verb: simplify means to make simple. A base verb follows 'to'.

gaps.sentence: The vaccine is still awaiting official ___ (APPROVE).
gaps.explanation: 'Official approval' — the noun form follows the adjective.

gaps.sentence: She gave a very ___ account of the incident that had everyone laughing (HUMOUR).
gaps.explanation: Everyone laughed, so the adjective is humorous (-ous). 'Humourless' means serious and would contradict the laughter.
